marks.gloss_en: מאי טעמא? אמר אביי: שבת קביעא וקיימא, יום הכפורים בי דינא דקא קבעי ליה
Abaye: Shabbat is fixed and established; Yom Kippur -- it is the court that fixes it
אלא אמר רבא: שמדא הוה, ושלחו מתם דיומא דכפורי דהא שתא שבתא הוא
אמר ליה רבא: סוף סוף תרוייהו בהדי הדדי קאתו -- unanswered; Rava offers his own account (אלא אמר רבא)
Rava: rather, it was a persecution, and they sent from there that Yom Kippur of this year is on Shabbat
ורבי יוסי הגלילי לית ליה איסור כולל? והתניא: שבת ויום הכפורים ... חייב על זה בעצמו ועל זה בעצמו ... דברי רבי יוסי הגלילי
שלח רבין משום דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: כך הצעה של משנה, ואיפוך (= p_eipoch)
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina (sent by Ravin): so is the presentation of the teaching, but reverse [the attributions]
Shabbat and Yom Kippur [together]: one who unwittingly did labour is liable for each by itself -- 'it is Shabbat', 'it is Yom Kippur'
R' Yochanan: per R' Yosei HaGelili as we reversed it -- unwitting as to Shabbat, deliberate as to Yom Kippur: liable
תניא, אמרו לו לרבי יהודה: is 'sons of Jacob' written? only 'sons of Israel', who were not so called until Sinai -- it was stated at Sinai and written in its place; the baraita records no reply
the Rabbis: is 'therefore the sons of Jacob shall not eat' written? only 'the sons of Israel', and they were not called 'sons of Israel' until Sinai
מתיב רבא: 'and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father' (Gen 46:5) -- called 'sons of Israel' before Sinai
לאחר מעשה -- that is after the incident
Rava: 'and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father' (Gen 46:5) -- they are called 'sons of Israel' before Sinai
Rav Acha b. Rava to Rav Ashi: מההיא שעתא ליתסר -- let it be forbidden from that hour
וכי תורה פעמים פעמים ניתנה? ההוא שעתא לאו שעת מעשה הואי, ולא שעת מתן תורה הואי -- was the Torah given time after time? that hour was neither the hour of the incident nor of the giving of the Torah
R' Yehuda (mishna, cited as the lemma): was the sciatic nerve not forbidden from the sons of Jacob, while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?
the prohibition of a limb from a living animal applies to domestic animals, wild animals and birds, non-kosher and kosher alike
R' Yochanan: both expounded one verse -- 'only be strong not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh' (Deut 12:23)
